commit_message:
Add support to defrag ebuckets incrementally (#13842)

In PR #13229, we introduced the ebucket for HFE.
Before this PR, when updating eitems stored in ebuckets, the lack of
incremental fragmentation support for non-kvstore data structures (until
PR #13814) meant that we had to reverse lookup the position of the eitem
in the ebucket and then perform the update.
This approach was inefficient as it often required frequent traversals
of the segment list to locate and update the item.

To address this issue, in this PR, This PR implements incremental
fragmentation for hash dict ebuckets and server.hexpires.
By incrementally defrag the ebuckets, we also perform defragmentation
for the associated items, eliminates the need for frequent traversals of
the segment list for defragging the eitem.

---------

Co-authored-by: Moti Cohen <moticless@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Copilot <175728472+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

findings.title: Use-after-free: hash key (keystr) dereferenced via dict lookup after owning kvobj is freed during active defrag
findings.message:
In activeDefragHExpiresOB(), `keystr` is captured as `kvobjGetKey(kvobj)` at the top of the function, i.e. it is a pointer into the memory owned by the original (pre-defrag) `kvobj` allocation. Later, the code calls `kvobj = activeDefragAlloc(kvobj)`. activeDefragAlloc() (see src/defrag.c, activeDefragAlloc) allocates a new copy of the object AND immediately frees the old pointer via zfree_no_tcache() when a move actually happens (i.e. when je_get_defrag_hint() indicates the allocation should be moved). After this call returns, the original `kvobj` memory (and therefore the `keystr` pointer that lives inside it) has already been released back to the allocator.

The very next statement, `link = kvstoreDictFindLink(db->keys, slot, keystr, NULL);`, dereferences/dereferences-through `keystr` (the dict uses the sds string key for hashing/compare) to locate the dictEntry for the key in db->keys. Because `keystr` points into freed memory, this is a use-after-free read: the freed chunk may have been reused by a concurrent/interleaved allocation inside the same defrag cycle (e.g. the zmalloc_no_tcache() call that created the new object, or any other allocation performed between the free and the lookup), causing kvstoreDictFindLink to hash/compare garbage data. This can lead to a failed lookup (serverAssert(link != NULL) crash), silent corruption of the wrong dict entry, or a straightforward heap-use-after-free that can be leveraged for information disclosure or further memory corruption depending on allocator behavior.

The bug is reachable whenever active defrag is enabled/triggered (e.g. `CONFIG SET activedefrag yes` with sufficient fragmentation, or `DEBUG MALLOC-STATS`/`DEBUG JMAP` style forced defrag cycles) and a hash key with field TTLs (HFE / hash-field-expire buckets, i.e. keys that appear in db->hexpires) becomes a defrag move candidate (je_get_defrag_hint returns non-zero for that kvobj's allocation). The HFE defrag stage (defragStageHExpires -> ebScanDefrag -> activeDefragHExpiresOB) then exercises exactly this path.
findings.suggestion: Do not free the old kvobj allocation until after keystr (and any other data derived from the old object) has been fully used to update the DB dict references. Split the allocate-and-free helper into an allocate-without-free step (activeDefragAllocWithoutFree) performed first, use keystr to locate/update the dict links against the still-valid old pointer, then explicitly free the old pointer only afterward (activeDefragFree). This is exactly what the upstream fix (commit d649637ebd1b7b7792a4224a42e1ef8824743378) does.

ground_truth.root_cause: activeDefragAlloc() couples allocation-of-replacement with freeing-of-original into a single call. activeDefragHExpiresOB() retained a reference (keystr) into the original object's memory for use after that call, not realizing the original memory had already been released by the time it performed the dict lookup/update. The ordering of free vs. use was inverted: the free needed to happen only after all derived pointers from the old object were no longer needed.
